items.headline: Qatar urges US and Iran to agree a deal to end the war
items.summary: Qatar's prime minister said both sides shouldn't wait for a 'perfect moment' to settle. Separately, President Trump confirmed new US strikes on Iran's Qeshm island.

items.headline: Paraguay's president removed and arrested
items.summary: Santiago Peña was impeached over links to the collapse of the digital lender Ueno, then detained. Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as president.

items.headline: Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff
items.summary: Miller replaces Susie Wiles in the top White House job, days after the US midterm elections.

items.headline: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%
items.summary: The first rise in more than three years, up from 3.75%, after renewed inflation pressure linked partly to high energy costs. Mortgage and savings rates may follow.

items.headline: Big tech sell-off hits markets, including the FTSE 100
items.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% on Thursday and chip stocks about 12%, on fears that the midterm results will slow data-centre building. Chips partly bounced back on Friday, but the FTSE 100 still closed about 1% lower.
items.source: AI Weekly (citing CNBC) and Yahoo Finance, 6 Nov

items.headline: US jobs growth comes in far stronger than expected
items.summary: The US added 165,000 jobs in October, well above forecasts. That pushed up bond yields and the chance of a US rate rise.

items.headline: Microsoft launches a 'container' to fence in AI agents
items.summary: Microsoft Execution Containers are now generally available. They use the operating system to limit what an AI agent on a computer can access, as companies give agents more access to data and tools.

items.headline: Mistral opens its managed AI agents to the public
items.summary: Mistral has a public preview of agents you can build with a visual workflow builder. Private-cloud and on-premises versions are due in late November.

items.headline: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab reportedly raising $5bn
items.summary: The AI start-up is reported to be raising $5bn led by Accel, at a $40bn valuation before the new money, roughly triple its value a year ago.
